speaker: Unknown
en: There's a very famous story about Canva.
zh: 有一个非常著名的故事关于 Canva。

speaker: Unknown
en: Early on, you pitched over a hundred investors and over a hundred investors said no to you.
zh: 在早期，你们向超过一百位投资者融资，并且超过一百位投资者对你们说了不。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really clear in my mind that it was the future and I thought the investors were wrong, frankly.
zh: 在我头脑里非常清楚那就是未来，而且我认为投资者们是错的，坦率地说。

speaker: Unknown
en: But investors also gave really helpful feedback and feedback.
zh: 但投资者们也给出了真正有帮助的反馈和反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often in the form of rejection, they would say, "Oh, your market's not big enough," and I would say, "It's going to be huge."
zh: 通常是以拒绝的形式，他们会说，「噢，你的市场不够大，」而我会说，「它将会是巨大的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd add a new page in my pitch deck that said how big the market I believe was, and then they'd say, "You're the same as some of other company."
zh: 然后我会在我的融资演示文稿中添加一页新纸，说我认为市场有多大，然后他们会说，「你们跟某些其他公司是一样的。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say, "Hey, now I've got a new slide in my pitch deck that shows all the players and the huge gap in the market that we believe we're going to fill."
zh: 而我会说，「嘿，现在我的融资演示文稿里有一张新幻灯片了，它展示了所有参与者以及我们相信我们要填补的巨大市场空白。」

speaker: Unknown
en: One of your values, Crazy Big Goals.
zh: 你们的价值观之一，疯狂大目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that as a value.
zh: 我很喜欢把它作为一个价值观。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
zh: 我关于疯狂大目标最喜欢的一点是，在它面前你会感到完全的不 adequacy。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to work really hard to will it into existence.
zh: 你想要非常努力地去工作以通过意志将其实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really like to start by just imagining what is the future that you actually want Right now?
zh: 我真的很喜欢从仅仅想象你真正想要的未来开始，就在此时？

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a wall in my house in my office, which is my vision for what I'd like the world to look like in 2050.
zh: 我在我家里的办公室有一面墙，那是我对 2050 年世界样貌的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard from one of your team members, Melissa Tan, there's a deck like this for every project you kick off.
zh: 我从你的一位团队成员 Melissa Tan 那里听说，对于你们启动的每个项目都有这样一个像这样的 deck。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this big vision deck.
zh: 有这个巨大的愿景 deck。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have this concept of chaos to clarity.
zh: 所以我们有这个从混乱到清晰的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every idea starts in the chaos side, and then you have to work all the way to the other side, which is clarity.
zh: 每个想法都从混乱的一侧开始，然后你必须一路工作到另一侧，也就是清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: That very first step at the far end of chaos was quite an embarrassing step actually, because you don't have mastery at that point.
zh: 在混乱最远端的那第一步其实是相当令人尴尬的一步，因为你在那个阶段还没有掌握能力。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Melanie, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Melanie，非常感谢你来到这里，欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for having me.
zh: 非常感谢你的邀请。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited to be here.
zh: 我很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm even more excited.
zh: 我更兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's such an honor to have you here.
zh: 很荣幸你能来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am such a fan of yours.
zh: 我真是你的超级粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm such a fan of the company that you've built.
zh: 我是你建立的公司的超级粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also just everyone I meet from Canva is just so nice and so awesome and so smart, and so clearly you've built something really special.
zh: 而且我遇到的每个来自 Canva 的人都非常好、非常棒、非常聪明，很明显你建立了一些真正特别的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited to use this hour to learn as much as I can from you about how you did that.
zh: 我真的很兴奋利用这一个小时尽可能多地向你学习你是如何做到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were actually chatting ahead of this about what would make the best use of this hour.
zh: 我们实际上在之前就聊过如何最好地利用这一个小时。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked you what you believe has been the biggest factor in the success of Canva.
zh: 我问你你认为 Canva 成功的最大因素是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You described something called building a Column B company and Column B thinking, I've never heard of this before, so let us start there.
zh: 你描述了一种叫做建立 Column B 公司和 Column B 思维的东西，我以前从未听说过这个，所以让我们从那里开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is building Column B company, what does that mean?
zh: 什么是建立 Column B 公司，那意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Really great place to start.
zh: 真是一个很好的起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I guess there's two ways of planning.
zh: 所以我想有两种规划方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that you can plan is you can dream of what is the perfect vision of the future, what future do you want to exist in, what would you like the world to look like?
zh: 你可以规划的方式是你可以梦想什么是未来的完美愿景，你想存在于什么样的未来，你希望世界看起来像什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you like companies to look like?
zh: 你希望公司看起来像什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then going from there, which is completely improbable, a completely crazy big dream, and then working hard to turn that into reality.
zh: 然后从那里开始，这完全是大概率不可能的，一个完全疯狂的大梦想，然后努力把它变成现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the alternate is, so just imagine you are building a castle on the hill and you're like, "What would be the most magical, wonderful, mythical experience?"
zh: 另一种选择是，所以想象你在山上建一座城堡，你想，“什么是最神奇、美妙、神话般的体验？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing you can do is you can look at the bricks around you and you can say, "What can I do with these bricks?
zh: 你可以做的另一件事是看看你周围的砖块，你可以说，“我可以用这些砖块做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: How high can I stack them?
zh: 我可以把它们堆多高？

speaker: Unknown
en: What can I do?"
zh: 我能做什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think most planning is often done by looking at the bricks and trying to stack them, and then you can create only so much.
zh: 我认为大多数规划通常是通过观察砖块并试图堆叠它们来完成的，然后你只能创造这么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I guess the column B thinking is thinking about what is that magical wonderful future that you then want to invest years and decades of your life actually building?
zh: 所以我想 Column B 思维是思考那个你想要真正投入数年甚至数十年生命去建立的神奇而美好的未来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's column A and column B in a nutshell.
zh: 所以这就是简而言之的 Column A 和 Column B。

speaker: Unknown
en: So column A is the traditional just work from today's world.
zh: 所以 Column A 是传统的只是从当今世界出发的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Column B is work from this dream reality and work backwards from how to achieve that.
zh: Column B 是从这个梦想现实出发并从如何实现这一点反向推导的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Exactly that.
zh: 正是如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is exactly the way actually Brian Chesky thought.
zh: 这实际上也是 Brian Chesky 的思维方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked at Airbnb for a long time and it was always just, "Think about the world, the dream and then work backwards from that," so there's a lot clearly also worked out.
zh: 我在 Airbnb 工作了很长时间，一直都是“思考世界、梦想，然后从那里反向推导”，所以显然也有很多做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So clearly this is an important lesson in the example of Canva, just what would've been column A for what Canva could have been and how did you think about the column B approach of what Canva in a dreamland could be?
zh: 所以显然这是 Canva 例子中的一个重要教训，只是 Canva 可能会有的 Column A 是什么，以及你如何考虑梦想乐园中 Canva 的 Column B 方法？

speaker: Unknown
en: So column A would've been nothing frankly, because the reality was when I was a university student with no company and no business or product or software experience, the reality would've been not very much.
zh: 所以坦率地说 Column A 什么都不是，因为现实是当我还是一个大学生，没有公司，没有商业或产品或软件经验时，现实不会是什么东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it was all column B, it was all thinking about the wild future that we wanted to create.
zh: 所以这全是 Column B，全是思考我们想要创造的狂野未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imagine what would be publishing in the future, what would communications look like in the future?
zh: 想象未来出版会是什么样子，未来的交流会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seemed really impossible that it would stay on the desktop, it would stay really complicated.
zh: 它仍然停留在桌面上、仍然非常复杂，这看起来真的不可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it just seemed so apparent to me that in the future it was going to be completely different.
zh: 对我来说，很明显在未来它将完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could I build that future?
zh: 我能建立那个未来吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I had absolutely no idea, but the idea, it seemed completely likely, completely improbable that it wouldn't be the case that in the future, design would be online and collaborative and really simple.
zh: 我完全不知道，但这个想法，似乎完全可能，完全大概率不可能的是，在未来设计不会是在线的、协作的和非常简单的，这不会是事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so starting from that, we then took that concept and applied it to the school yearbook market in Australia with our first company Fusion Books.
zh: 所以从那时起，我们接受了这个概念并将其应用于澳大利亚的校刊市场，也就是我们的第一家公司 Fusion Books。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we applied it to Canva where we wanted to take it much, much bigger.
zh: 然后我们将其应用于 Canva，因为我们想要把它做得大得多，大得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's talk about just how to actually go about building a Column B company.
zh: 让我们谈谈实际上如何着手建立一家 Column B 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say a founder is listening to this and they're just like, "Okay, I want to do this."
zh: 假设有一位创始人在听这个节目，他们就像，“好吧，我想做这个。”

speaker: Unknown
en: What do they do?
zh: 它们是做什么的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What are the steps?
zh: 有哪些步骤？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where do you start?
zh: 你从哪里开始？

speaker: Unknown
en: I really like to start by just imagining what is the future that you actually want?
zh: 我真的很喜欢从仅仅想象那个你真正想要的未来开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the world that you want to live in?
zh: 那个你想要生活在其中的世界是什么样的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the future of transportation?
zh: 交通的未来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the future of healthcare?
zh: 医疗的未来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the future that you want to live in and exist in?
zh: 那个你想要生活和存在的未来是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And for example, right now I have a wall in my house in my office, which is my vision for what I'd like the world to look like in 2050.
zh: 例如，现在我家办公室里有一面墙，那是关于我希望 2050 年的世界是什么样子的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's not necessarily that you can bring that into existence or you can will that into existence, but just to start to get clearer on what you would like that world to be like.
zh: 所以不一定是说你能让它成真，或者你能凭意志让它成真，而仅仅是开始对你希望那个世界是什么样子变得更清晰一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you like it to be more inclusive?
zh: 你希望它更具包容性吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you like it?
zh: 你希望它……

speaker: Unknown
en: For me, one of the things I desperately want is everyone on this planet to have their basic human needs met.
zh: 对我来说，我非常渴望的事情之一是，这个星球上的每个人都满足基本的人类需求。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are those things that you believe are so important that you would love to see exist in that future?
zh: 哪些是你认为如此重要、以至于你希望在那个未来中看到存在的事物？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think an exercise we often do is what is wild success for X, or what is wild success for Y?
zh: 我认为我们经常做的一个练习是，对于 X 来说什么是巨大的成功，或者对于 Y 来说什么是巨大的成功？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then equally, what is terrible failure for those things?
zh: 然后同样地，对于这些事情来说什么是彻底的失败？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can apply that just to abstract thinking in different industries.
zh: 你可以将其应用于不同行业的抽象思维。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can do that, apply that.
zh: 你可以这样做，应用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do that for the whole company for different areas of the company.
zh: 我们为整个公司的不同领域做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think just taking that very long timescale of 10 years and getting a really crisp idea of what you want, of what you don't want, that's sort of the first step.
zh: 我认为只要采取那个非常长的时间尺度，即 10 年，并对你想要的、你不想要的东西获得一个非常清晰的想法，这就是第一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of people don't spend quite enough time imagining that.
zh: 我认为很多人没有花足够的时间去想象这一点。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 然后下一部分是，你不想只有这个疯狂的大梦，却对把它变为现实无所作为。

speaker: Unknown
en: You kind of want to have a ladder that goes all the way up to the moon, which is your crazy, wild vision.
zh: 你想要有一架梯子，一直通到月球，那是你疯狂的、狂野的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you want to have rungs that just work its way up step by step.

en: And so you want to get that really clear picture of the future that you would like and then just take little step, after little step, after little step.

speaker: Unknown
en: And it doesn't matter how small that first step is or how seemingly inconsequential if it is working towards that future that you want to will into existence, then you'll keep on climbing up that ladder in the right direction.
zh: 第一步有多小，或者看起来多么微不足道并不重要，只要它是朝着你想要凭意志实现的那个未来努力，你就会继续沿着那个梯子在正确的方向上攀登。

en: I know where I'm going.

speaker: Unknown
en: I have this big idea."
zh: 我有这个大主意。”

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think they might be missing about just what this actually means and why they're probably not thinking big enough, they're not making the time to think this.
zh: 你认为他们可能错过了关于这实际意味着什么的什么，以及为什么他们可能想得不够大，他们没有花时间去思考这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is easy to be discouraged by the two, because they're completely two complete odds.
zh: 我认为很容易因为这两者而感到气馁，因为它们完全处于两个极端。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're completely different ends of the spectrum.
zh: 它们是光谱中完全不同的两端。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is dreaming about the future, not that you think you can will into existence, it's just the future that you want.
zh: 所以一个是梦想未来，不是你认为你能凭意志实现的那个未来，只是你想要的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the next part is taking the tiny step that might be extremely microscopic and it feels a little embarrassing to be like, "I want a future that is," whatever it might be.
zh: 然后下一部分是迈出可能极其微小的那一小步，感觉有点尴尬，比如说，“我想要一个这样的未来，”不管是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then to take such a microscopic step because I think you often have the future in one side or don't spend much time thinking about that.
zh: 然后迈出如此微观的一步，因为我认为你通常一方面拥有未来，或者不花太多时间思考那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're just thinking about the bricks before you.
zh: 你只是在思考你面前的砖块。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it's also naturally we all get distracted by day-to-day.
zh: 所以我认为也很自然地，我们都会被日常事务分散注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's your email, your Slack, the things that are kind of in your face, the reality that lives around you every day that kind of pulls you into this moment right now.
zh: 它是你的邮件、你的 Slack，那些就在你面前的事情，那些每天围绕在你身边、把你拉回到当下的现实。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我认为实际上真正花时间去思考这一点可能是最关键的部分之一。

zh: 就是字面上梦想 10 年后什么是巨大的成功，10 年后什么是彻底的失败，这是一个非常好的起点，就是花点时间在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then even if that is so big and so vast and so wild, having that very first step is so important because then you take that little tiny first step and then the next step then that compounds for us, it's been compounding over a decade as we continue to work towards that same mission and vision.
zh: 然后即使它是如此宏大、如此广阔、如此狂野，拥有那第一步也是如此重要，因为随后你迈出那微小的第一步，然后下一步，然后这对我们来说是复合的，随着我们继续朝着相同的使命和愿景努力，这已经复合了十年多。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to hear how you operationalize this.
zh: 我想听听你是如何将这一点的。

zh: 我从你的团队成员之一 Melissa Tan 那里听说，你启动的每个项目都有这样一套幻灯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this big vision deck.
zh: 有这个大愿景幻灯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about what that looks like, because I think that's where people are like, "Okay, how do I actually do this?"
zh: 谈谈它是什么样子的，因为我想这就是人们会想，“好吧，我实际上该怎么做这个？”

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about that deck.
zh: 谈谈那套幻灯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have this concept of chaos to clarity and every idea starts in the chaos side, and then you have to work all the way to the other side, which is clarity.
zh: 所以我们有这个从混乱到清晰的概念，每个想法都始于混乱的一面，然后你必须一路走到另一面，那是清晰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so chaos can be an idea, it can be a problem, it can be a philosophy or a belief.
zh: 所以混乱可以是一个想法，它可以是一个问题，它可以是一种哲学或信仰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've got a joke that I find funny.
zh: 我有一个我觉得很好笑的笑话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure if you will, but how do you go from chaos to clarity?
zh: 我不确定你会不会，但你如何从混乱走向清晰？

zh: 你增加清晰度。

zh: 所以这个想法是，从混乱到清晰的每一个小步骤，第一步可能实际上就是把它写下来。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 下一步可能是开始完善它，把它变成一些设计，变成原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then as it kind of goes from chaos to clarity, it starts to become more and more real and more and more people can see it.
zh: 然后随着它从混乱走向清晰，它开始变得越来越真实，越来越多的人可以看到它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so just taking those little incremental steps that adds clarity with every single step, then starts to help will it into existence rather than it being something that's completely amorphous and just stays in your head.
zh: 因此，只需要采取那些微小的增量步骤，每一步都增加清晰度，然后开始帮助将其意愿化为现实，而不是让它成为一个完全无形的东西，只停留在你的脑海中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's why visual communication for us is so important, is because otherwise, if it's just in your head, no one else can see it and you can't will it into existence.
zh: 所以我认为这就是为什么视觉沟通对我们如此重要，因为否则，如果它只是在你脑海中，没有其他人能看到它，你也不能将其意愿化为现实。

zh: 这让我想起了埃德·卡特姆尔写的书《创意公司》中的「丑陋婴儿」这个概念，他在书中谈到新想法就像一个没人想看和处理的丑陋婴儿，我想他说他们想扼杀它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know why you would do that with an ugly baby.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind what I'm hearing here is have this big vision that many people are be like, "No, wait.

zh: 我喜欢这个想法，「好的，但这是我们可以采取的一步，看看这是否能成真。」

speaker: Unknown

zh: 是的，我完全同意。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我认为关键在于，在混乱的最远端的那第一步是非常令人尴尬的，因为你会想，「我有这个如此宏大和狂野的想法，我到底该怎么做？

zh: 你还没有所有答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ideally you get the idea that it would be so cool that you want to work really hard to will that into existence.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我认为其中一个真正关键的部分不仅是拥有这个想法，而且认为它是如此酷，以至于你将工作数年将其意愿化为现实。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that that's the great thing about a pitch deck, is that other people can see your thinking and your thinking actually gets clarified as well as you go through that process.
zh: 所以我认为这就是演示文稿的伟大之处，其他人可以看到你的想法，而且当你经历那个过程时，你的想法实际上也得到了澄清。

speaker: Unknown
en: I talked to Melissa, I talked to a bunch of other people that work at Canva, that have worked at Canva, and something else I heard along these lines is this phrase, Crazy Big Goals, which I think is one of your values.
zh: 我和梅丽莎谈过，我和在 Canva 工作的一群其他人谈过，还有曾在 Canva 工作过的人，我听到的另一件与此相关的事情是「疯狂大目标」这个词组，我认为这是你们价值观之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Crazy Big Goals.
zh: 疯狂大目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that as a value.
zh: 我喜欢作为一种价值观这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is that so important?
zh: 为什么这如此重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that fit into this?
zh: 它是如何融入其中的？

speaker: Unknown

zh: 仅仅谈谈拥有疯狂大目标的力量。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我的意思是，那就是疯狂大目标的缩影。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 如果我们再进一步宏观来看，我们有一个两步计划，建立世界上最有价值的公司之一，并做我们能做的最多的善事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, a rather crazy big goal.
zh: 所以，又是一个相当疯狂的大目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the thing that I love about a crazy big goal is that you feel completely inadequate before it.
zh: 我认为我喜欢疯狂大目标的一点是，你在它面前感到完全的不胜任。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another crazy big goal.
zh: 另一个疯狂的大目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'd love to see everyone's basic human needs met on the planet.
zh: 我们希望看到地球上每个人的基本人类需求得到满足。

zh: 完全疯狂的大，这真的不应该。

zh: 但我认为对于疯狂大目标，你会想非常努力地工作将其意愿化为现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you start with a reasonable goal or a realistic goal, then you kind of get to it and you're like, "Oh cool, whatever."
zh: 所以如果你从一个合理的目标或现实的目标开始，那么你会达到它然后你会说，「哦，酷，无所谓。」

speaker: Unknown

zh: 或者更重要的是，如果发生了什么，所有的问题和障碍随之而来，就像它们经常做的那样，那么你会说，「好的，我不去费那个劲了。」

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can just go and choose another course.
zh: 然后你就可以去选择另一条路线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a crazy big goal is both crazy big, but it's also something that you think is incredibly important that you actually want to will into existence because it is so much work to will a crazy big goal into existence.
zh: 所以一个疯狂大目标既疯狂又大，但它也是你认为非常重要的东西，你实际上想要将其意愿化为现实，因为将一个疯狂大目标意愿化为现实需要如此多的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it better be one that you want to actually achieve.
zh: 所以它最好是你真正想要实现的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a crazy big goal that you set that comes to mind maybe as a good example of, "This is what I'm talking about?"

speaker: Unknown

en: And so every year we're just launching more and more things to fulfill that part of the mission of empowering everyone to design anything.

speaker: Unknown
en: And then equally in every language we started in English and then it was Spanish and then it was 20 languages and then a hundred languages and then hard languages like Arabic and Hebrew and Urdu and right to left languages.
zh: 然后同样在每种语言中，我们从英语开始，然后是西班牙语，然后是 20 种语言，然后是一百种语言，然后是像阿拉伯语和希伯来语和乌尔都语这样的难懂语言，以及从右到左的语言。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以你可以看到，拥有这些非常宏大、大胆的目标，然后你一步一步地朝着它前进，这有助于凭意志让它存在，或者在每一个设备上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We started off obviously just with a web platform and then we launched our iPad app and then iPhone and then Android and then we spent years investing in cross-platform.
zh: 我们显然只是从 Web 平台开始，然后我们推出了我们的 iPad 应用，然后是 iPhone，然后是 Android，然后我们花了好几年投资于跨平台。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以我们在每个设备上都有相同的功能集。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以你可以看到这些巨大的无形的东西看起来非常离奇，然后你可以在十年的持续投资后凭意志让它存在，它随着时间的推移而复合。

zh: 有这个宏大的疯狂雄心勃勃的愿景，下面有向这个愿景输送的使命支柱，然后是每个使命支柱中的疯狂大目标，来衡量你在所有这些使命组成部分方面的进展。

en: Exactly, exactly.

zh: 我回顾我们在 2021 年制作的 2021 年愿景卡片，显然是在 2021 年制作的，但它是关于 2026 年的，看到我们实际上能够从那个愿景卡片中实现多少东西以及有多少事情目前仍在进行中是非常迷人的。

zh: 然后有点像我们开始做这些叫做赛季揭幕战的事情，赛季揭幕战真的很有趣，我们把整个公司聚集在一起，我们谈论我们实现的目标。

zh: 这很有趣，因为在赛季揭幕战之前，每个人都会发布所有东西，因为他们想在赛季揭幕战之前做完。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we'd also set the goals for the coming cycle for the coming season at that point in time.
zh: 然后我们还会在那个时候为接下来的周期、接下来的赛季设定目标。

zh: 所以试图找到那种平衡，在保持同样的每个人都要有深度上下文的哲学、保持同样的庆祝和目标的哲学的同时，在每一个规模化阶段找到那种合适的味道，确实是很难的。

zh: 所以我认为这只是一个持续进行的工作。

zh: 它至关重要是因为由于代码库的组织结构方式，我们在任何时候只能让五个人在我们的编辑器中工作，我们以为这需要六个月，然后它花了两年，这是一个产品公司两年没有发布任何产品的两年，一个产品公司两年无法发布产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we didn't really know how long it was going to take because it just had to take as long as the tunnel was going to take.
zh: 我们真的不知道这需要多长时间，因为它只需要花费隧道那么长的时间。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So then when people, the first time I remember I spoke to someone for hours and they eventually got it.

speaker: Unknown
en: They were really committed to understanding what we were trying to do, but then not everyone has six hours to understand a concept.
zh: 他们真的很努力去理解我们要做的事情，但并不是每个人都有六个小时去理解一个概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so being able to take all the gems of wisdom from that conversation and have that understood really clearly in a really short period of time and have all of the reasons that people were rejecting us pre-answered in that initial pitch deck was really important.
zh: 所以能够从那次对话中汲取所有智慧的结晶，并在很短的时间内让人清楚地理解，并且在最初的融资演讲稿中预先回答人们拒绝我们的所有理由，这真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's probably one of the reasons why when I look back at our 2012 pitch deck, it's so valid and really still captures what we're doing today.

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that rejection in some ways makes you stronger if you can persist through.

en: It's not just persisting, it's actually iterating and taking feedback that you're hearing to continue to evolve the pitch to a place where, "Okay, I finally get what you're doing."

en: That is such a cool part of the story.

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your general advice to folks that are having a hard time fundraising?
zh: 对那些在筹集资金方面遇到困难的人，你的一般建议是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I can only go on my experience, but I think it's sort of the dark tunnel analogy.
zh: 我的意思是，我只能根据我的经验来说，但我认为这有点像黑暗隧道类比。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or chaos to clarity, let's go with that one.
zh: 或者从混乱到清晰，我们就用这个吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a slightly friendlier analogy and I think just taking the rejection and turning into things that you can control.
zh: 这是一个稍微友好一点的比喻，我认为就是把拒绝转化为你可以控制的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I can control my pitch deck, I can control the number of people I'm speaking to and I just spoke to literally everyone.
zh: 所以我可以控制我的融资演讲稿，我可以控制我要交谈的人数，实际上我和每个人都谈过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that continuing to use it to refine it rather than taking it as a personal rejection, I think it's really important to think how can I improve?
zh: 我认为继续用它来改进它，而不是把它当作个人的拒绝，我认为思考如何改进是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can I help someone to understand it?
zh: 我怎样才能帮助某人理解它呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Some people are never going to understand it.
zh: 有些人永远不会理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember pitching an investor that had the lean startup book behind them when I was pitching them and they were never going to like Canva.
zh: 我记得向一位投资者做融资演讲，他们身后放着《精益创业》这本书，他们永远不会喜欢 Canva。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were not the lean startup.
zh: 我们不是精益创业。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was not the way that we were approaching it whatsoever.
zh: 那根本不是我们的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's some people that are just going to never like you and that's okay.
zh: 所以有些人就是永远不会喜欢你，这没关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's important to find some people that do what you're trying to say and trying to do and kind of finding your tribe, I think.
zh: 我认为重要的是找到一些人在做你想说的和想做的一番事业，并且找到你的部落，我认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: As an investor, this is really interesting to hear because it tells you there are companies like Canva there that everyone's turning down, a hundred investors passed on, that you might still be able to invest in.
zh: 作为投资者，听到这个真的很有趣，因为它告诉你，像 Canva 这样的公司，大家都拒绝了，100 位投资者拒绝了，你可能仍然能够投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talking about your growth as a leader, say if you compare Melanie of today to Melanie of, I don't know, 12, 13 years ago when you were just starting Canva, what would you say is most different in terms of leadership?
zh: 谈谈你作为领导者的成长，比如说如果你比较今天的 Melanie 和 12、13 年前刚开始创办 Canva 时的 Melanie，你认为在领导力方面最大的不同是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't really know.
zh: 我真的不知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably if you ask other people around me, they'd probably be more observant.
zh: 如果你问我周围的人，他们可能会观察得更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it is funny because there's some things that I think that I need to change and then I realize you go into it the same as some other company.
zh: 但这很有趣，因为有些事情我认为我需要改变，然后你意识到你进入它就像其他一些公司一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes we even try that for a while and then we try that out and we're like... It didn't really work for us.
zh: 有时我们甚至尝试了一段时间，然后我们尝试了一下，然后我们就像……这对我来说真的没用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind of building a house that you want every brick in the house to match.
zh: 这有点像建房子,你希望房子里的每一块砖都相匹配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you go and try and take some bricks from someone else's house and stick it in your house, it's probably going to not look very matched.
zh: 如果你去尝试从别人的房子里拿一些砖并把它们粘进你的房子,它看起来很可能不太搭配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so trying to find things that are authentic to us and are authentic to everything that's come before it, is just that constant, constant thing.
zh: 所以试图找到对我们来说是真实的东西,并且对它之前的一切也是真实的,就是那种持续的、持续的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then each scale of each stage of scale of the company rather than going, taking someone else's bricks and trying to stick that in your house, trying to build the thing that's authentic.
zh: 然后对于公司规模的每个阶段,而不是去拿别人的砖并试图把它粘进你的房子,而是试图构建那个真实的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's many things that are the same, but obviously the stage and scale and we're constantly having to give away hats.
zh: 所以我认为有很多事情是相同的,但显然阶段和规模,我们要不断地把帽子送人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you kind of think about it in the very early days.
zh: 所以你会想到在很早的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just a few of us, two of us in Fusion and then three of us in a little tiny group, and you kind of wear a hundred hats and then you have to be able to give away those hats to other people that can then do that way better than yourself.
zh: 我们就几个人,在 Fusion 有我们两个,然后在一个小群体里有我们三个,你会身兼数职戴一百顶帽子,然后你必须能够把这些帽子送给其他人,然后他们能比你做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm sure there's been a few skills I guess I would've had to have developed over the last decade to be able to give away those hats.
zh: 所以我肯定有一些技能我想我必须在过去十年里培养出来,以便能够送出那些帽子。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, I think there's a lot of things that we've had to do and double down on that was more authentic to the way we did it in the early days actually.
zh: 但是是的,我认为我们必须做很多事情并加倍下注,这对我们在早期实际做事的方式来说更真实。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that story.
zh: 我喜欢那个故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think again, if anyone working at a company that has gone through a lot of growth has experienced that when people from other companies come in and, "Here's how we did it at this company."
zh: 我认为同样地,如果任何一家在经历了大量增长的公司工作的人,都会经历过这种情况,当来自其他公司的人进来时说,“这就是我们在这家公司做事情的方式。”

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there an example of some there that just like, "Here's something that this company brought in and people from this company thought we should do and we try it and didn't work?"
zh: 那里有没有什么具体的例子,就是“这家公司带进来了某样东西,来自这家公司的人认为我们应该这样做,我们试了但没奏效?”

speaker: Unknown
en: I won't go into specific examples, but so many times over.
zh: 我不会去说具体的例子,但是有很多很多次。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that, I mean maybe that's probably, in answer your other question, we did things our way because that was the only way we knew.
zh: 而且我认为,我是说也许那可能就是,回答你的另一个问题,我们以我们自己的方式做事,因为那是我们知道的唯一方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there was many, many times over the years that we didn't have confidence in the way we were doing things and we were like, "Oh, they've done it from a big company that's bigger than our company.
zh: 而且在这些年里有很多很多次,我们对我们做事的方式没有信心,我们就像,“噢,他们是从一家比我们公司大的大公司那样做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go do that."
zh: 让我们那样做吧。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that hasn't always worked out so well for us.
zh: 那样做对我们来说并不总是结果很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so yeah, I think confidence in how we take what is authentic to us and do it at the next level of scale is a constant work in progress.
zh: 所以是的,我认为对于我们如何采用对我们来说是真实的东西并在下一个规模层面上做这件事的信心,是一项正在进行的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like, as I was saying before, systems break and need to be reinvented but also reimagined for that next layer of scale rather than going to try to get something off the shelf from another company.
zh: 感觉就像,正如我之前说的,系统会崩溃并需要被重新发明,但也需要为下一个规模层面重新构想,而不是去尝试从另一家公司获得现成的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine it also helped that you were in Australia away from the Bay Area and where all these other big companies are at, just being able to do it your own way.
zh: 我想这也很有帮助,你在澳大利亚,远离湾区和所有这些其他大公司所在的地方,能够以你自己的方式做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, very much so.
zh: 是的,非常如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you know that I have a whole team that helps me with my podcast and with my newsletter?
zh: 你知道我有一个整个团队帮助我处理我的播客和我的简报吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I want everyone on that team to be super happy and thrive in the roles.
zh: 我希望那个团队里的每个人都在他们的角色中超级快乐和兴旺。

speaker: Unknown
en: JustWorks knows that your employees are more than just your employees, they're your people.
zh: JustWorks 知道你的员工不仅仅是你的员工,他们是你的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: My team is spread out across Colorado, Australia, Nepal, West Africa and San Francisco.
zh: 我的团队分布在科罗拉多、澳大利亚、尼泊尔、西非和旧金山。

speaker: Unknown
en: My life would be so incredibly complicated to hire people internationally to pay people on time and in their local currencies and to answer their HR questions 24/7.
zh: 如果我必须在国际上雇佣人、按时用当地货币给他们发薪、并 24/7 回答他们的人力资源问题,我的生活将会非常难以置信的复杂。

speaker: Unknown
en: But with JustWorks, it's super easy whether you're setting up your own automated payroll, offering premium benefits or hiring internationally.
zh: 但是有了 JustWorks,这超级简单,无论你是设置你自己的自动薪资处理、提供高级福利还是在国际上雇佣。

speaker: Unknown
en: JustWorks offer simple software and 24 7 human support from small business experts for you and your people.
zh: JustWorks 为你和你的团队提供简单的软件和来自小企业专家的 24 7 人工支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: They do your human resources so that you can do right by your people, JustWorks, for your people.
zh: 他们为你做人力资源工作,这样你就可以善待你的人,JustWorks,为你的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else that is a good example of how you did something pretty different from how other companies operate?
zh: 还有其他什么例子是你如何以与其他公司运营方式相当不同的方式做事的好例子吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything else that comes to mind as a fun example?
zh: 还有什么其他事情作为一个有趣的例子出现在脑海中?

speaker: Unknown
en: The goal driven structure, I think the things that we were talking about before.
zh: 目标驱动的结构,我认为我们之前谈论的那些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the mission, actually breaking that down into the mission pillars, breaking those mission pillars down into the goals that we're then pursuing and then celebrating those goals when we do achieve them, I think is a deeply underloved way of building a company.
zh: 所以是使命,实际上把它分解为使命支柱,把那些使命支柱分解为我们随后追求的目标,然后当我们实现它们时庆祝那些目标,我认为这是一种深受低估的构建公司的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often people have a mission that's kind of on the wall somewhere and then what they're actually doing and the way they actually make money and the way people actually spend their time is in a very, very different direction from that original mission.
zh: 通常人们有一个使命,它贴在墙上的某个地方,然后他们实际做的事情和他们实际赚钱的方式以及人们实际花费时间的方式,是与那个最初使命非常、非常不同的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the magic is when you can bring those two things together and so you can have your mission, you can have your mission pillars that actually are helping to achieve that.
zh: 我认为神奇之处在于当你能够把这两件事结合在一起,所以你可以拥有你的使命,你可以拥有你的使命支柱,它们实际上有助于实现那个使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a real authenticity in that for customers as well, is that you are actually doing the thing that you promised you do, and it all ladders up together.
zh: 我认为对于客户来说也有一种真实感,就是你在实际做你承诺你会做的事情,而且这一切都串联在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's certainly not an easy way to run a company, but I think that when you do get that formula, I think that there's a lot of authenticity with what you're saying you're doing, you're actually doing.
zh: 这当然不是一种经营公司的简单方式,但是我认为当你确实得到那个公式时,我认为在你的说你要做的事情和你实际做的事情之间有很多真实性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to come back to that.
zh: 我想回到那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a whole really cool process.
zh: 那是一个非常酷的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have with closing the loop with customers, but something else I want to talk about while we're in this topic of growth over time.
zh: 你有与客户形成闭环,但还有我想在我们在关于随时间增长的这个话题时谈论的其他事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw you post something about how you had to realize they had to slow down and not just work, work, work like crazy.
zh: 我看到你发布了关于你如何意识到他们必须慢下来,而不仅仅是疯狂地工作、工作、工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just that realization and why that ended up being so valuable.
zh: 谈谈那个意识到这一点以及为什么那最终变得如此有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the early days, I would just work seven days a week round the clock.
zh: 所以在早期,我只是七天全天候工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our very first company, we actually had printing presses because we were printing the yearbooks in my mom's house and then delivering them to schools around Australia.
zh: 在我们的第一家公司的最早期,我们实际上有印刷机,因为我们在我的妈妈的房子里印刷年鉴,然后把它们送到澳大利亚各地的学校。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in the early days of Canva, we certainly were working all weekend, all hours of the day.
zh: 在 Canva 的早期,我们确实在周末工作,在一整天里的所有时间工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just constant.
zh: 它只是持续不断的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you've been doing this for a while, if you just keep working at that pace, I don't think it's good for anyone's health, mental health or anything else.
zh: 但是当你做这件事有一阵子了,如果你只是保持那个节奏工作,我认为这对任何人的健康、心理健康或其他任何事都不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think finding ways to continue, I still work extraordinarily hard, but to continue to have that balance in my day to day where I actually go to sleep, I find time to do things like going for walks or doing yoga, journaling I find extraordinarily helpful to make sure that I can always bring my best to everything that I'm doing.
zh: 所以我认为找到方法继续,我仍然工作非常努力,但是继续在我的日常生活中拥有那种平衡,我实际上去睡觉,我发现时间去做像散步或做瑜伽、写日记这样的事情,我发现这非常有帮助,以确保我总能把我的最好状态带给我正在做的所有事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easy to say that kind of stuff.
zh: 说出那种话很容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: It must be really hard to actually make time for that thing.
zh: 实际上为那件事腾出时间肯定真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything for those sorts of things, is there anything that you do that allows you to actually protect that time to actually do these things?
zh: 对于这类事情有什么办法吗，你有没有做什么事情让你能够真正保护这段时间去真正做这些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because as you said, there's a billion things that are just looking for your attention constantly.
zh: 因为正如你所说，有十亿件事情一直在寻找你的关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like I've developed some healthy habits over the years.
zh: 我觉得这些年来我养成了一些健康的习惯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't have emails on my phone and so when I shut my laptop, I actually tune out and then if there's a real issue, I'll get an emergency call or page.
zh: 我的手机上没有邮件，所以当我合上笔记本电脑时，我真的会切断联系，如果真的有问题，我会接到紧急电话或传呼。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think trying to delineate I think is really important.
zh: 但我认为试图划清界限真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I'm working, I'm all in and then when I'm not working, I'm all out.
zh: 所以当我工作时，我全力以赴，当我不工作时，我完全抽离。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually giving that mental space I think is really important.
zh: 我认为真正给予那种心理空间真的很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've spoken to a lot of founders that haven't quite found that and then do struggle with it.
zh: 我和很多创始人谈过，他们还没有完全找到这一点，并且确实为此感到挣扎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when they're working every weekend it feels like the right thing, but then sometimes you can miss the forest from the trees when you're just working harder and harder, but maybe you're actually working on the wrong thing.
zh: 所以当他们每个周末都在工作时，这感觉像是正确的事情，但有时当你只是更加努力地工作时，你可能会只见树木不见森林，或者你可能实际上在错误的事情上工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think being able to step away a little just to be able to get perspective is actually really beneficial.
zh: 所以我认为能够稍微抽离一点，以便能够获得视角，实际上是非常有益的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to come back to this closing the loop process.
zh: 我想回到这个闭环流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say that you have where you figure out what to build.
zh: 假设你已经弄清楚了要构建什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of your ideas come actually from the community.
zh: 你的很多想法实际上来自社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about just that process and how many of your ideas actually came from your community.
zh: 请谈谈这个流程，以及你的想法有多少实际上来自你的社区。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, it's one of my favorite things.
zh: 噢，这是我最喜欢的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been doing it for years now, and so we get more than a million requests from our community every year and we've got a whole incredible team that then tallies them, breaks them down, and then delivers them to all of our product teams and then those actually get closed.
zh: 我们已经这样做好几年了，所以我们每年从社区收到超过一百万个请求，我们有一整个了不起的团队来统计它们，分解它们，然后交付给我们所有的产品团队，然后这些实际上得到闭环。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this year we've closed more than 200 loops, but we know that each one of those things is going to be loved and needed by so many more people that don't bother to actually fill out the request form.
zh: 所以今年我们已经闭环了超过 200 个循环，但我们知道，每一个这样的东西都会被许多更多的人所喜爱和需要，但他们懒得真正填写请求表。

speaker: Unknown
en: So many things from gradient text, like little things like gradient text to really big things like our Sheets product.
zh: 从渐变文本这样的小东西，到我们的 Sheets 产品这样真正大的东西，有太多的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's just been countless products.
zh: 有无数的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the early days with our AI products, we didn't release them to teachers because we knew there was a lot of hesitancy for teachers using AI in the classroom.
zh: 在早期，对于我们的 AI 产品，我们没有向教师发布，因为我们知道教师在课堂中使用 AI 有很多犹豫。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we got so many requests from teachers saying, "Can I please use this MagicWrite in the classroom?"
zh: 我们收到老师的很多请求，说“我可以在课堂上使用这个 MagicWrite 吗？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so with them we unlocked that and put on safety controls for teachers.
zh: 所以我们为他们解锁了它，并为老师添加了安全控制。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's just constant, actually.
zh: 所以它实际上是持续的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just part of our product process.
zh: 它只是我们产品流程的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's two parts to product.
zh: 我认为产品有两个部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is building the future and towards the mission and the mission pillars as I was saying before.
zh: 一个是构建未来，朝着使命和我之前说的使命支柱前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other is actually listening to our community and building what they want.
zh: 另一个是真正倾听我们社区的声音并构建他们想要的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that that's the two core pieces of product in my mind.
zh: 所以我认为这就是我心目中产品的两个核心部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the closing the loop comes in so many different forms.
zh: 闭环有多种形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the explicit asks, and then the other thing that we double down on all the time is user testing and watching people use it.
zh: 有明确的请求，然后我们要加倍投入的另一件事是用户测试，观察人们如何使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if people hesitate clicking a button or people don't quite understand how something works, it's amazing to me how you can find 10 random people on the internet and they can give such astute feedback that then is so representative for such a large number of people.
zh: 如果人们在点击按钮时犹豫，或者人们不太明白某事是如何运作的，我觉得很神奇，你可以在互联网上找到 10 个随机的人，他们可以给出如此敏锐的反馈，然后能够代表如此多的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've personally run hundreds if not thousands of user tests myself and it's been deeply embedded in our product teams also.
